title: IceHacks
summary: IceHacks 2026 is a free virtual student hackathon hosted by CodeStarters where you can build software, apps, games, or hardware projects.

flags.title: Pages contradict whether cash prizes are awarded
flags.explanation: The overview explicitly states multiple times that no cash prizes are awarded, but the prize list itemizes specific cash prize amounts totaling over $17,000 across multiple categories.

evidence.quote: IceHacks doesn't award any cash prizes. All prizes are sponsor credits, subscriptions, scholarships, and other non-cash rewards.
evidence.context: IceHacks doesn't award any cash prizes. All prizes are sponsor credits, subscriptions, scholarships, and other non-cash rewards.

evidence.quote: $150 in cash
evidence.context: $150 in cash

flags.title: The demo video is required on one page but optional on another
flags.explanation: The overview states that a demo video link is strictly required and unsubmitted projects will not be judged, while the rules page states the demo video is optional.

evidence.quote: Projects without a working video link will not be judged.
evidence.context: Demo video (required): a public YouTube, Vimeo, or Youku link, 3 minutes or less, showing your project working. Explain the problem, show the demo, and briefly say how you built it. Projects without a working video link will not be judged.

evidence.quote: A demo video under three minutes is optional but recommended.
evidence.context: Project Demonstration: A working prototype or demonstration is required. A demo video under three minutes is optional but recommended.

flags.title: The rules page requires a GitHub repo, but overview allows a live link
flags.explanation: The rules page mandates that every submission must include a public GitHub repository, whereas the overview requirements state you may provide either a public GitHub repo or a live demo link.

evidence.quote: Every submission must include a public GitHub repository.
evidence.context: Project Repository: Every submission must include a public GitHub repository.

flags.title: Anakin Scale prize is a partial discount rather than fully free access

openQuestions.question: Are college or university students allowed to compete?
openQuestions.why: The rules page specifies high school students only, but the Devpost overview welcomes students aged 13+ generally.

openQuestions.question: Are cash prizes actually distributed to winners, and how?
openQuestions.why: The main page banner claims no cash prizes are awarded, despite cash dollar amounts listed under almost every track.

openQuestions.question: Can projects be entered into other hackathons or competitions simultaneously?
openQuestions.why: The rules do not mention dual-submission policies or exclusivity for other concurrent events.
